public_rationale: The STAC paper by AWS AI Labs and UC Berkeley researchers was revised on arXiv on 2 February 2026. That version reports that agents including GPT-4.1 are highly vulnerable to sequential tool-chaining attacks, with success rates above 90% in most cases. The new Elloe-led study reports a similar 91% tool-chaining vulnerability. GovInfoSecurity says the AWS/UC Berkeley researchers documented the same dynamic in an earlier February paper. One small caveat: STAC first appeared in September 2025, so 'February' refers to its revised version.
limitations: Marcus does not name the February paper; it is identified as STAC by inference.
STAC first appeared in September 2025, not February 2026.

our_interpretation: Holds if a paper by AWS and UC Berkeley researchers, released or revised in February 2026, documented agent vulnerabilities similar to the new study's, such as multi-step tool-chaining attacks.
'Amplifies' is read as the new study reporting consistent findings at larger or production scale. It is not a strict causal claim.
criteria.support_condition: An AWS/Berkeley paper dated February 2026 reports high agent vulnerability to tool-chaining or similar attacks, and the new study reports similar vulnerabilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No such AWS/Berkeley paper exists from around February 2026, or its findings concern unrelated vulnerabilities.
